questions.question: Which part of a cell controls its activities and contains genetic material?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains DNA and controls what the cell does.

questions.question: Which of these is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts (where photosynthesis happens) are only in plant cells. Plant cells also have a cell wall and a permanent vacuole.

questions.question: What is the job of the cell membrane?
options: Controls what enters and leaves the cell
questions.answer: Controls what enters and leaves the cell
questions.explanation: The membrane controls movement of substances in and out. The cell wall (in plants) keeps the cell rigid.

questions.question: What is the correct order of organisation, from smallest to largest?
questions.explanation: Similar cells form a tissue, tissues form an organ, and organs work together as an organ system.

questions.question: In which state are particles closest together and only vibrating on the spot?
questions.explanation: In a solid the particles are tightly packed in a fixed arrangement and can only vibrate.

questions.question: What is the name for a liquid changing into a gas at its boiling point?
questions.explanation: Boiling is liquid → gas at the boiling point. Condensing is the reverse: gas → liquid.

questions.question: Why can a gas be squashed (compressed) but a solid cannot?
options: There are big spaces between gas particles
questions.answer: There are big spaces between gas particles
questions.explanation: Gas particles are far apart, so pushing them closer together is possible. Solid particles are already touching.

questions.question: Which method would you use to get salt back from salty water?
questions.explanation: Heating the solution evaporates the water and leaves the salt crystals behind. Filtration cannot remove a dissolved solid.

questions.question: Sand is mixed with water. Which method separates them best?
questions.explanation: Sand does not dissolve, so it is trapped by filter paper while the water passes through.

questions.question: A solution has a pH of 2. What is it?
questions.explanation: pH below 7 is acidic; the lower the number, the stronger the acid. pH 7 is neutral; above 7 is alkaline.

questions.question: What is produced when an acid reacts with an alkali?
questions.explanation: This is neutralisation: acid + alkali → salt + water.

questions.question: What is the unit of force?
questions.explanation: Forces are measured in newtons, using a newtonmeter (force meter).

questions.question: A box has a 10 N force pushing it right and a 4 N friction force to the left. What is the resultant force?
questions.explanation: Opposite forces subtract: $10 - 4 = 6$ N, in the direction of the bigger force (right).

questions.question: Why does an astronaut weigh less on the Moon than on Earth, even though their mass is the same?
questions.explanation: Weight = mass × gravitational field strength. Mass stays the same, but the Moon's gravity is about one sixth of Earth's.

questions.question: A battery-powered torch is switched on. Which energy store is being emptied?
questions.explanation: The battery's chemical store is emptied; energy is transferred electrically and by light (and some by heating).

questions.question: Which of these is a renewable energy resource?
questions.explanation: Wind will not run out. Coal, oil and gas are fossil fuels and are non-renewable.

questions.question: Why do we see lightning before we hear the thunder?
options: Our eyes are faster than our ears
Light travels much faster than sound
questions.answer: Light travels much faster than sound
questions.explanation: Light travels at about 300 000 km/s; sound in air only about 340 m/s.

questions.question: Sound cannot travel through which of these?
questions.explanation: Sound is a vibration passed between particles. A vacuum has no particles, so sound cannot travel through it.

questions.question: A student tests how the height of a ramp affects how far a car rolls. What is the independent variable?
questions.explanation: The independent variable is the one you change on purpose. The distance rolled is the dependent variable you measure.

questions.question: Why should you repeat an experiment several times?
options: To check results are repeatable and spot anomalies
questions.answer: To check results are repeatable and spot anomalies
questions.explanation: Repeating lets you calculate a mean, spot odd results and check your results are reliable.
